text: Given a definition with ordinary fields across two pages and no data-source/tenant-scoped choices, When exported then imported, Then the imported definition equals the source definition except for the (new) form ID.

Given a real form with "requires Microsoft 365 sign-in" enabled plus non-default progress-bar/thank-you-message settings, When exported then imported on INT, Then all three settings match on the imported form.
steps: On INT, open or create a form with "requires Microsoft 365 sign-in" enabled, show-progress-bar on, and a custom thank-you message
Switch to a second INT tenant and call mspbots_forms_form_import(export_payload) with the resulting JSON
Call mspbots_forms_form_get on the new form_id with include=["definition"] and compare the three settings
expect: The imported form's "requires Microsoft 365 sign-in", progress-bar, and thank-you-message settings are identical to the source form's
notes: needs a real multi-tenant INT form; cannot be reproduced as a pure-function unit test since this server has no local database

text: Given a real form with at least one submitted response, When imported, Then the imported form has 0 responses.
steps: On INT, use a source form that has at least one submitted response
Export then import it into a second tenant as in TC2
Call mspbots_forms_response_summary (or response_list) on the new form_id
expect: 0 responses on the imported form, regardless of how many the source form had
notes: needs a real INT form with existing responses

text: Given a definition with one question using choicesByUrl, When strip_tenant_specific runs, Then that question has no choicesByUrl and no choices, and the report lists it with reason "data-source-bound".

Given a definition with a client_org-style question whose static choices are objects carrying tenantId/haloClientId/rewstOrgId, When strip_tenant_specific runs, Then choices is cleared and the report lists the question with the matched key names.

Given a definition with an ordinary question whose static choices are plain strings (no tenant-shaped keys), When strip_tenant_specific runs, Then the question is returned unchanged and does not appear in the report.

Given an export payload with export_version 2 (or missing), When mspbots_forms_form_import is called, Then it returns an invalid_argument error naming the unsupported version and client.post/client.patch are never invoked.
Given a successful import, Then the returned object contains form_id and a report key (empty list when nothing was flagged).

Given strip_tenant_specific runs on a definition built under a simulated tenant-A fixture carrying known tenant-A-only identifiers, When the result is asserted against, Then none of those identifiers survive un-flagged in the output.
tests/test_tools.py::test_tools_list_snapshot passes with 16 tools including the two new ones and their expected required-params/annotations.

Given a definition with a client_org-style question whose static choices live under choicesSource.items (items carrying tenantId/haloClientId/rewstOrgId nested inside an "attrs" dict) instead of a top-level choices list -- the real shape confirmed live on sibling ticket PRD-21379 -- When strip_tenant_specific runs, Then choicesSource is dropped, choices is cleared, and the report lists the question with the matched key names.

Given the exported form record carries a status field (and an owner/sharing-shaped field), When imported, Then neither reaches the PATCH body, while an ordinary sibling setting (e.g. showProgressBar) still does.

Given a source form whose raw SurveyJS definition carries its own top-level "title" key (the real-world shape -- round 1's SOURCE_FORM fixture omitted it), When mspbots_forms_form_import runs, Then the "title" key inside the definition handed to the PATCH call equals the suffixed new title (source title + title_suffix), not the source's original title -- so the backend cannot re-derive the stored/displayed title from the nested definition and silently discard the " (imported)" suffix (COV1: the tool's own echoed return value already said the right title, but the stored title equalled the source's because the PATCHed definition's own title field still carried the old value).

Given a definition with a question whose choices live under "choicesSource" and whose items carry no TENANT_SCOPED_CHOICE_KEYS match (the externally/dynamically-sourced shape QA-NIGHT found live on INT, as opposed to the cached-static-items shape TC11 already covers), When strip_tenant_specific runs, Then that question is still treated as data-source-bound: "choicesSource" is dropped, "choices" is cleared, and the question appears in the report -- same unconditional treatment as choicesByUrl, not conditioned on a tenant-key match (COV2: the round-1 code only stripped choicesSource when a tenant-scoped key happened to match, so a live data-source choicesSource with no such key stayed bound and unreported, and its source parameters were carried into the destination tenant unflagged).

Given a form whose full record (definition + questions + versions) serializes to more than dump_json_capped's 20,000-char budget (e.g. 80 questions / ~34KB, the size class QA-NIGHT reproduced and this ticket's own PRECICOM/Ginko-sized target forms fall into), When mspbots_forms_form_export runs, Then the returned payload's "form" key is the complete, untruncated record -- no "truncated"/"omitted_fields" keys and no dropped "form" field -- because export output is saved to a file for a later import, not consumed as agent-facing conversation context, so the generic token-budget cap must not apply to it (FIND1: the generic dump_json_capped helper shed the entire "form" field for oversized forms, since a dict export envelope has no list-shaped field for the existing truncation path to shrink instead).

Given an export_payload whose "form" key is missing, empty, or marked truncated/omitted (e.g. a payload produced by the FIND1 bug before its fix, or any other producer of a malformed envelope), When mspbots_forms_form_import is called, Then it refuses with a clear invalid_argument error and makes no post/patch call -- never silently creating an empty "Untitled form" (FIND1's second half: import's own validate_export_version check only looks at export_version, so a structurally-incomplete "form" silently passed through and produced an empty shell form).
